content:
jen: quick heads-up — ran an end-to-end p95 perf sweep on the canary and host-side parse/tokenization cost spiked (~+28% p95). attaching notes and a tiny flame excerpt.

liam: link to dashboard? :eyes:

jen: https://perf.redwood.internal/dash/host-canary/1781818181 — top-level looks like lots of small chat payloads on http2 multiplexed streams.

jen: perf top snapshot (host cpu hot functions):
```
parse_tokenize               28.7%
grpc_writev                  12.3%
kv_cache_eviction             9.4%
socket_flush                 7.8%
kernel_selector_soft_path    6.5%
```

sasha: kernel_selector_soft_path — that usually means the runtime fell back to the soft kernel for short sequences. Did kernel weights change on canary?

arun: also curious about batching hint config — if lots of tiny requests hit, we could be creating many tiny minibatches and losing kernel throughput.

jen: canary diff: batching_hint=auto (previously = manual with target=8), prefix_cache was disabled (memory cap tweak), and http2 multiplexing + writev coalesce was NOT enabled (proxy change missed). so three simultaneous changes.

maya: the prefix_cache disable will cause more KV lookups and evictions — matches the kv_cache_eviction line. I expect hit-rate dropped.

liam: concrete experiments to run (cheap, canary-safe):
  1) force kernel_pref=fast_small_seq on 10% canary nodes
  2) enable writev_coalesce on http2 proxy path
  3) re-enable prefix_cache with capped LRU (lower mem but keep prefix hits)
  4) temporarily set batching_hint=manual,target=8 for short-chat routes

sasha: +1. also add per-request kernel telemetry (small counter: kernel_id used) — low overhead, helps verify fallback freq.

jen: ran a tiny synthetic locally: enabling writev_coalesce reduced number of grpc write syscalls by ~60% and host CPU p95 by ~9% for short chat workload. kernel change was needed too — soft kernel still dominated when batchsize==1.

arun: can we add a quick microbenchmark: varying batch sizes [1,4,8,16] with short seqs (<32) and record kernel latency + tokens/sec? if we can show the knee at 8 that's a good justification for manual hint.

perf-bot: scheduled trace collection job "host-canary-kernel-check" across 10 nodes at 1781818200.

maya: i'll repro the kv-cache toggles locally and post hit-rate numbers. i expect hit-rate to go from ~78% -> ~92% when prefix cache is re-enabled.

jen: proposal for canary patch: enable writev_coalesce + kernel_pref override + rollback batching_hint to manual for customer-facing routes; keep prefix_cache re-enabled with LRU bleed. collect 1h perf and flame. owners: liam / sasha / maya.

liam: i'll open the roll PR and tag infra-oncall. will push the writev change to the proxy first (should be harmless).

sasha: add regression alert: host_parse_p95 > +10% from baseline -> block deploy, and create a dashboard showing kernel selection distribution.

jen: thx — i'll attach the quick flame and the synthetic scripts in the PR. :thumbsup:

liam: timeline: roll to 10% in 30m, collect 1h, evaluate.

maya: posting initial kv hit-rate after repro in ~20m.

jen: thanks everyone. we'll iterate on observability and make kernel selection telemetry permanent.

sasha: also file a follow-up to consider automatic batching hints based on request histograms — long-term fix.

jen: noted — filing ticket after the canary run.
